text:
sam (support): urgent — ACME reports production JSON.parse failures after we promoted model v6.1 to canary. Their consumer gets intermittent invalid shapes: sometimes the API returns a top-level "items" array, other times the same response is wrapped in a "result" object. Failing downstream parsing with 'Unexpected token r'. Customer started seeing errors ~2024-09-21 22:03 UTC, ~5% of requests.

elena (eng-runtime): can you paste the exact raw response body they receive and the request id + model tag?

sam (support): pasted from their logs (redacted):
```
{"id":"abc123","result":{"items":[{"id":1,"name":"foo"}]}}
```
and sometimes it is:
```
{"id":"abc123","items":[{"id":1,"name":"foo"}]}
```
Not consistent across calls. They call chat.complete with structured_output=true and stream=false.

jordan (eng-ml): hmm. sounds like a post-processing unwrap/normalize step flipping based on some runtime heuristic. any routing flags in logs?

sam (support): request_id=rQwZ-99, route=acme-orders, model=redwood/v6.1-q4f. Relevant log line: `WARN postproc: wrapper_detected True; unwrap_policy='auto'`

elena (eng-runtime): there's a rollout note for v6.1 that enabled an 'auto_unwrap' optimization to handle some legacy webhooks — @aiops-bot can you confirm where that flag was toggled?

aiops-bot: rollout r-2024-09-21 enabled auto_unwrap for redwood/v6.1 in eu-west-1 (deployed by @deploy-bot).

jordan (eng-ml): hypothesis: the postproc uses a heuristic that behaves differently on cache-hit vs cache-miss or when a particular batch boundary triggers chunked postprocessing. If cache hits take a faster path we might leave items unwrapped; cache-miss goes through new unwrap routine and inserts "result". That would explain intermittent schema drift.

elena (eng-runtime): mitigation plan: 1) disable auto_unwrap on the acme-orders route (sam can you toggle?), 2) gather a raw capture of a failing HTTP response (tcp dump or raw body from our proxy), 3) add an integration test hitting cache-hit and cache-miss paths to reproduce.

sam (support): toggled route config to `unwrap_policy=off` at 22:18 UTC. Customer reports failures stopped within 2 minutes. They provided the raw failing body capture and I uploaded to the incident ticket.

jordan (eng-ml): i'll open a PR to change the heuristic to deterministic behavior (model contract wins). I will also add explicit canary tests to exercise both cached and uncached paths. Assigning to eng-runtime for review.

elena (eng-runtime): please also ensure rollout gating — auto_unwrap can't be turned on by default for general traffic. Add a feature-flag and safety check that it can't be enabled for routes marked 'strict-schema'.

sam (support): customer OK with the temporary mitigation. they're asking for timeline for a permanent fix and a postmortem.

jordan (eng-ml): ETA for PR + tests: 2 business days, then canary, then rollback if regressions. I'll include test vectors from ACME's payloads.

elena (eng-runtime): we'll follow up with a short postmortem template, include kpi: % of calls affected, change that caused behavior, and mitigations (feature-flag + deterministic postproc).

sam (support): thanks team — customer is relieved. will update ACME and close the urgent alert once we have PR link. :thumbsup:

aiops-bot: Incident created INC-2024-3099 assigned to eng-runtime.

Notes: reproducibility hint — look at `postproc.unwrap_policy='auto'` + routing config that enables streaming even when client sets stream=false (optimizations for batching/routing may flip a runtime flag). This was the root cause in the captured traces. Keep structured-output contract deterministic.
